points.text: Urbanisation is the increase in the proportion of a country's population living in urban areas (towns and cities) rather than rural areas (1 mark). It is caused by rural-urban migration (people moving from countryside to city) and natural increase (births exceeding deaths within urban populations) (1 mark).

questions.question: Explain how push and pull factors contribute to rural-urban migration. (4 marks)

points.text: Push factors drive people away from rural areas - low agricultural wages, lack of services (healthcare, education, electricity), drought and famine, and lack of employment opportunities (1 mark). For example, in many LICs, rural farmers earn less than $2 per day, pushing them to seek better incomes in cities (1 mark). questions.question: Why are most megacities now located in LICs and NEEs? (6 marks)

points.text: Most megacities are now in LICs and NEEs because these countries are experiencing the most rapid urbanisation (1 mark). HICs are already highly urbanised (over 75%) and their urban growth has slowed, meaning their cities grow slowly if at all (1 mark). questions.question: "Natural increase is a more significant cause of urban growth than migration." To what extent do you agree? (9 marks)

points.text: I agree that natural increase is very significant, accounting for approximately 60% of urban population growth in LICs and NEEs (1 mark). This is because migrants are predominantly young adults of childbearing age, leading to high urban birth rates (1 mark).
